findings.claim: Across the full observed score window [0.0,0.49], the read landmark-00 and landmark-10 displacement and soft-mass curves show no accepted polynomial trend (polynomial_accepted=false for all eight), with multiple sign changes (4-10) and strong sign conflicts (1-13) per feature; whole-window z magnitudes are small (|z|<=0.64). This is consistent with oscillatory, batch-conflicted coordinate motion rather than a monotone drift, so no stable whole-window direction is established for these features.

Endpoint rate contrasts are large and opposite in sign between window ends for several features: landmark_00_local_dx first_rate_z=-17.49 vs last_rate_z=+8.11; landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z=-72.37 vs last_rate_z=+5.52; landmark_10_local_dx first_rate_z=-42.98 vs last_rate_z=+11.39; landmark_10_soft_mass first_rate_z=+66.28 vs last_rate_z=-11.56. These are endpoint rate contrasts within the observed support, not absolute coordinate targets or spatial gradients.

landmark_00_soft_mass is the only read feature with a positive whole-window mean (whole_window_z=+0.64) and the lowest relative node RMSE (0.286) among the eight read curves, but it still has 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict, so its positive whole-window level is not a clean monotone trend.

hypotheses.direction: weaker early, stronger late (test the registered early-soft dose recipe)
hypotheses.falsifier: If the early-soft recipe does not change the primary final-affinity metric relative to the incumbent, or if the per-node rate contrast is not reproducible across independent batches, the timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: Per-node endpoint rate z of landmark_00_local_dx and landmark_10_local_dx across observed score nodes 0.0-0.49
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window; no extrapolation beyond 0.49
hypotheses.statement: If the early portion of the observed window carries a distinct coordinate regime, then a dose schedule that reduces guidance weight at early score nodes and redistributes it to later nodes (as in the registered early-soft recipe) should be tested against the incumbent; the observed early-vs-late endpoint rate sign reversals in landmark_00_local_dx and landmark_10_local_dx are the temporal contrast motivating this test.

hypotheses.direction: stronger mid-window (test the registered middle-peak dose recipe)
hypotheses.falsifier: If the middle-peak recipe does not change the primary final-affinity metric relative to the incumbent, or if the mid-window soft-mass peak is not reproducible across independent batches, the timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: Per-node soft-mass z of landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_10_soft_mass across observed score nodes 0.0-0.49
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window; no extrapolation beyond 0.49
hypotheses.statement: If the middle of the observed window is where coordinate motion is most active, then a middle-emphasis dose schedule (registered middle-peak recipe) should be tested; the mid-window peaks in landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_10_soft_mass values_z near nodes 0.14-0.21 are the temporal contrast motivating this test.

limitations: Only 8 of 200 catalogue curve features were read (landmark_00 and landmark_10 displacement and soft-mass); the remaining 192 features are unqueried, not absent.
No stage profiles or temporal profiles are available; only continuous per-node curves were used.
All read curves have polynomial_accepted=false and multiple strong sign conflicts, so no stable whole-window monotone direction is established for any read feature.
Endpoint rate contrasts are within-window contrasts and do not specify an absolute coordinate target, spatial gradient, or optimal guidance dose.
Descendant final quality and decoded final affinity are not observed in this role input; selection preference is association only, not measured benefit.
The registered dose recipes (W1/W2/W3) are hypotheses about timing, not discovered stages; no knot stability analysis was performed.
